THE OWNER'S RULING IS IMPLEMENTED ON ALL FOUR SIBLINGS AND THE SWITCH IS REAL. EVAL.curve_period, DOM.manage_period, FAB.manage_period and MEM.rekey_period now each refuse a negative value of their OWN lever, naming the lever and the value, raising the spine's LeverError (spine/lever.py), and firing BEFORE units.Windows is constructed -- so nothing is derived from the bad value. CKPT.save_period's existing refusal was brought under the same switch.

RECOMMENDATION, AND IT IS NONE OF THE THREE AS WRITTEN: option (b) WITHOUT THE LEVER. The switch is REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD, a module-level constant with a full docstring, one per owning package, in the same file that raises. It is (b)'s ownership shape at none of (b)'s price.
(a) IS UNAFFORDABLE AND I DID NOT SPEND AN EDGE. A RUN-owned switch read by five packages is FIVE wires against six remaining -- and I established, rather than assumed, that the accessors CANNOT read it wire-free: O1 forbids naming os.environ, O8 forbids from_env, O10 restricts a package to spine.{lever,units,derive,rng,wire,gate,init} and forbids importing another package, and Config.owned_by refuses a foreign Config at the read site. A NEW spine module holding one flag is refused by O10's ALLOWLIST (tests/test_ownership.py:1526) until someone widens it -- an edit to tests/, not to a package.
(b) AS WRITTEN LOSES ON PRICE AND ON WHAT THE PRICE BUYS: five environment names, five census rows and five docs/04_LEVERS.md rows for ONE decision, and five independent env-settable switches make 'three accessors refuse and two do not' a reachable configuration. It is also the WORSE instrument for the measurement that would settle the question, because spine/lever.py latches the assembly after one build -- a lever switch needs a fresh process per arm; the constant flips in one. And it was not implementable this round in any case: no levers.py is in my ownership line.
(c) LOSES ON THE OWNER'S OWN SECOND SENTENCE AND ON D4. Its practical cost is that 'does the refusal have a bad effect' could then only be answered by maintaining two trees.
WHAT THE CHOSEN SHAPE COSTS, PLAINLY: turning it off is a CODE EDIT, not a shell variable -- an operator with only a terminal cannot reach it. There is no census row and no docs/04_LEVERS.md row. The name is spelled FIVE TIMES because O10 forbids the four siblings to import CKPT's copy; they are five per-package policies sharing a default, each governing only its own lever. And this is the FIRST switchable refusal in the tree -- lm/api.py::resolve, opt/api.py::build and capacity/api.py::new_valve all refuse out-of-range levers with no switch -- so each copy says in as many words that it is NOT a precedent, only what the owner asked for by name.

NONE of the four already refused and none was structurally unable to receive a negative: all four ended in a bare `return U.Windows(int(<lever>))`, and I MEASURED each accepting -1000, -5 and -1 through assemble.build before touching them.

findings.detail:
THE WORST OF THE FOUR TO HAVE LEFT UNREFUSED, and the split is readable in this file rather than imagined for it. MEM_REKEY_EVERY drives TWO mechanisms: MEM.maintain's internal amortized re-encode, armed on `rekey_every > 0`, and the spine's dom.rekey gate through RUN.Cadences.due, whose contract is elapsed-since-last-fire. At a NEGATIVE value the two mechanisms read the SAME number in OPPOSITE directions -- maintain treats it as DISARMED (the store silently stops tracking the model as it drifts, which is a forgetting mechanism and therefore goal B) while the dom.rekey event fires every single window. docs/04_CONTRACT.md already names this field as 'one lever, two mechanisms, two gates, one ledger key'; a value that makes the two mean opposite things is exactly what a range check at the first read is for, and the refusal message states the contradiction in full.
PLACEMENT: this is the FIRST read but not the only one, and the comment says so -- the accessor is called at the `cadence` row of ASSEMBLY_ORDER, maintain is a LOOP_ORDER row, so the refusal still precedes every derivation from the bad value in this package.
ZERO IS PRESERVED EXACTLY: maintain declares 0 as DISARM behind a guard, recording that the old tree documented 0 as the off switch and then divided by it. The test is strictly `< 0`, so that off switch is untouched -- which is the point, since the negative range is the one with no declared meaning at all.
findings.repro: BEFORE: MEM_REKEY_EVERY=-1000/-5/-1 -> Windows(-n), cannot_fire=[('dom.rekey', -n, 0)] -- the same line shape printed for the value the store treats as DISARM. AFTER: LeverError naming the lever, the value and both mechanisms; 0 -> Windows(0), cannot_fire=[('dom.rekey',0,0)] unchanged; 1 and 200 unchanged; switch False reproduces the before run exactly. The two-reader split is in this file: memory/api.py::maintain clause 2 reads 'If key_src == "model" and rekey_every > 0' while RUN.Cadences.due reads 'True at most once per `period` WINDOWS elapsed since this key last fired'.

findings.detail:

A module-level constant, True as shipped, consulted by save_period's existing guard; the four siblings each declare a constant of the same name in their own file, because O10 forbids them to import this one. Its docstring carries, in one place: the ruling verbatim; the D4 ground; an explicit statement that it is NOT a precedent that range refusals get switches (lm/api.py::resolve, opt/api.py::build and capacity/api.py::new_valve all refuse with no switch); the three weighed shapes with each loser's price; the cost of the winner stated rather than discovered (a code edit, no census row, no environment name, the name spelled five times); the reachability limit measured in fresh processes; and the falsifier -- if any configuration this project runs ever sets a period negative ON PURPOSE, this becomes a lever and option (b) is then right.
IT ALSO MADE AN EARLIER ROUND'S CHOICE LOAD-BEARING, and I recorded that at the line: CKPT's armed-but-0 Gate reason was made an f-string 'because a sentence that is true only because of a guard somewhere else is a sentence that goes false the day the guard moves'. That day is this edit. With the switch False a negative reaches that arm again and it renders 'CKPT_EVERY=-5' beside '(-5 vs 1)'. Under the literal the line used to carry, turning the refusal off would have restored the exact false equation the refusal was written to end. Two other statements in ckpt/api.py that were true only while the guard was unconditional -- the DID IT FIRE line's '0 is the only value that can reach that arm' and the gate-arm comment's copy of it -- are now qualified with the switch.
findings.repro: scratchpad/f/after.py sweeps 5 accessors x 6 values x both switch positions = 60 cells in one process (the constant is flipped by assignment; a lever could not be, because spine/lever.py latches the assembly after one build). Switch True: 15 negative cells raise LeverError, 15 others identical to the before run.
